recommendations.title: NON-DESTRUCTIVE RULE
RUN AND INSPECT EVERYTHING FIRST
recommendations.text:
============================================================

Before changing architecture:

A. Read:
- README.md
- CHANGELOG.md
- all architecture documents
- methodology documents
- governance documents
- production/release documents
- schemas
- templates
- source registries
- validation scripts
- publication build scripts
- Studio
- book reader
- records
- assets
- downloadfiles

B. Explicitly inspect:

downloadfiles/ebookcraft/
downloadfiles/ebookcraft (1)/

Treat ebookcraft (1) as the newer comparative design unless evidence
inside the project establishes otherwise.

Also inspect all reference imagery in downloadfiles, including the
Walter Russell / alternative-periodic-arrangement references.

These files are design/research references.
Do not blindly copy copyrighted artwork into MAT.
Determine what concepts need original MAT-designed replacements.

C. Run the existing MAT application and build pipelines.

Use the repository's own commands where applicable:

npm ci
npm run validate
npm test
npm run build:book
npm run build:publication
npm run check:studio
npm run test:studio
npm run test:e2e

Run MAT Studio.

Run the existing book reader.

Run ebookcraft and ebookcraft (1) separately if their dependency
manifests permit it.

Use browser automation / Playwright.

Capture desktop, tablet and mobile screenshots.

Test at minimum:
- wide desktop;
- normal laptop;
- portrait tablet;
- landscape tablet;
- modern mobile portrait;
- narrow/mobile accessibility viewport;
- print/paperback preview;
- A4/PDF preview.

Do not evaluate the UI only by reading CSS or React code.

Interact with it.

Click the menus.
Expand/collapse the tree.
Open several elements.
Open domain/sub-records.
Search.
Bookmark.
Use evidence views.
Try read-aloud.
Try print mode.
Try export mode.
Try keyboard navigation.
Resize the viewport.
Check long tables.
Check equations.
Check images.
Check citations.
Check mobile navigation.
Check focus states.

Produce BEFORE screenshots for later comparison.

============================================================

recommendations.title: TRACE THE ACTUAL DATA PIPELINE
recommendations.text:
============================================================

Trace one complete record from filesystem to browser.

Start with:

records/0000-Origin-State/

Then:

records/0001-Hydrogen-H/

Follow:

source Markdown/YAML
    ->
schema validation
    ->
registries
    ->
relationships
    ->
build scripts
    ->
publication model
    ->
book/index assets
    ->
Studio loader
    ->
frontend rendering
    ->
export formats

Document exactly:

WHERE the canonical fact lives;
WHERE its prose explanation lives;
WHERE citations live;
WHERE relationships live;
WHERE visual assets live;
WHICH generated files depend on it;
WHICH files must never be hand-edited.

If there are duplicated authorities, identify and remove ambiguity
without deleting useful content.

Canonical fact ownership must be unambiguous.

============================================================

recommendations.title: AUDIT RECORD COMPLETENESS
PRESERVE THE MAT CORE RECORD MODEL
recommendations.text:
============================================================

The MAT record remains the scientific parent object.

Example:

MAT:0001 = Hydrogen

Hydrogen must NOT become separate contradictory copies for chemistry,
physics, biology, medicine, aerospace, etc.

Instead use:

ONE CANONICAL KNOWLEDGE CORE
+
MULTIPLE DOMAIN VIEWS
+
MULTIPLE READING DEPTHS.

The canonical object owns facts.

Domain pages reference, filter, interpret and extend those facts.

============================================================

recommendations.title: ADD A DOMAIN-LENS ARCHITECTURE
recommendations.text:
============================================================

MAT is intended for essentially every field that uses matter or
materials.

DO NOT hard-code only:
"chemistry, physics, biology".

Create an extensible DOMAIN REGISTRY / TAXONOMY.

Potential domain families include, but are not limited to:

- chemistry
- physics
- nuclear science
- quantum science
- materials science
- biology
- biochemistry
- medicine
- pharmacology/pharmaceuticals
- toxicology
- environmental science
- geology
- geochemistry
- astronomy
- astrophysics
- planetary science
- energy
- electrical engineering
- electronic engineering
- mechanical engineering
- chemical engineering
- civil engineering
- structural engineering
- aerospace
- automotive
- marine
- manufacturing
- metallurgy
- ceramics
- polymers
- composites
- semiconductor engineering
- nanotechnology
- photonics
- optics
- acoustics
- magnetics
- thermal engineering
- cryogenics
- plasma engineering
- robotics
- computing
- AI/ML
- simulation
- data science
- laboratory practice
- industrial processes
- agriculture
- food science
- textiles
- construction
- mining
- recycling
- conservation
- archaeology
- history of science
- education
- safety
- regulation
- metrology
- standards

Do not create empty folders for thousands of combinations.

Use a registry-driven model.

A domain becomes visible for an element when that domain has meaningful
content or relationships.

Allow new domains to be registered without altering every element schema.

============================================================
6. ELEMENT HOME PAGE = FRONT DOOR
============================================================

Every element/material needs a calm, professionally edited overview.

The home page should orient the reader without dumping the entire
scientific record.

For an element such as Hydrogen, provide:

- identity;
- symbol and atomic number;
- concise description;
- natural/material manifestation;
- why it matters;
- where it occurs;
- major forms/states;
- headline physical/chemical properties;
- key applications;
- key hazards;
- major scientific relationships;
- discovery/history summary;
- evidence/quality status;
- links to deeper domains;
- key visuals;
- related records;
- primary sources.

Then allow the user to enter deeper specialist views.

The overview should work for:
- a general reader;
- a school student;
- a researcher orienting themselves;
- an AI retrieving a high-level summary.

It must not replace technical depth.

============================================================

recommendations.title: ADD A REAL NARRATIVE / HISTORY LAYER
EVIDENCE LANES — ABSOLUTELY PRESERVE ALL REFERENCE MATERIAL
BUILD A FIRST-CLASS KNOWLEDGE GRAPH AND LINK SYSTEM
recommendations.text:
============================================================

Do not rely on ad-hoc Markdown hyperlinks.

Create or strengthen a typed entity/relationship/link registry.

Internal entities include:

ELEMENT
ISOTOPE
ION
MOLECULE
COMPOUND
MATERIAL
ALLOTROPE
PHASE
PROCESS
REACTION
ENVIRONMENT
APPLICATION
EXPERIMENT
EQUATION
CONSTANT
PROPERTY
SPECTRUM
FREQUENCY
MODEL
THEORY
CLAIM
PERSON
ORGANIZATION
PATENT
PAPER
BOOK
DATASET
STANDARD
VIDEO
WEBSITE
IMAGE
ARCHIVE
SOURCE

A mention of Hydrogen in another MAT record should be capable of
resolving to MAT:0001.

The renderer should support automatic or authored entity links without
rewriting the same URL everywhere.

Examples:

Hydrogen
→ internal MAT Hydrogen record.

A scientist/researcher
→ MAT person entity + appropriate authoritative external biography or
primary source.

A paper
→ DOI / publisher / repository.

A patent
→ patent identifier and authoritative patent registry where publicly
accessible.

Wikipedia
→ direct relevant article, treated as a tertiary reference rather than
a primary scientific authority.

YouTube/video
→ direct exact video, channel/creator metadata, topic relationship and
access date.

Dataset
→ exact dataset landing page/API/DOI.

Standard
→ exact standards organization record when permitted.

============================================================

recommendations.title: CENTRAL SOURCE / LINK REGISTRY
recommendations.text:
============================================================

A URL should not have to be manually changed in 40 element files.

Expand the existing source registry where appropriate.

Each source should support fields such as:

source_id
source_type
title
author/person IDs
organization
publication
date
edition/version
DOI
ISBN
patent_number
URL
archive_URL
accessed_date
language
rights/licence
primary/secondary/tertiary
peer_review_status
evidence_relevance
notes
replacement_source
link_status
last_checked
content_hash where legal/useful

Do not require every field for every source type.

Use typed schemas.

============================================================

recommendations.title: SIDE CITATIONS / MARGIN CITATIONS
recommendations.text:
============================================================

Implement proper scientific citation UX.

A fact/paragraph/table/chart/equation/image should be able to carry
fine-grained source references.

Desktop:
- margin/side citations where space allows.

Tablet/mobile:
- inline expandable citation markers / footnote sheet.

Print/PDF:
- footnotes/endnotes/reference list according to publication style.

EPUB:
- accessible EPUB note semantics.

AI:
- fact → source IDs must remain machine traversable.

Citation hover/tap preview can show:

- source title;
- author;
- year;
- evidence type;
- source type;
- DOI/link;
- data condition;
- provenance status.

Do not obscure reading with enormous citation blocks.

============================================================

recommendations.title: LINK HEALTH
recommendations.text:
============================================================

The repository already has link validation.

Strengthen it into source-health management.

Detect:

OK
REDIRECTED
BROKEN
TIMEOUT
PAYWALLED
REMOVED
ARCHIVED
UNKNOWN

When an external link dies:
- do not erase historical citation identity;
- preserve metadata;
- try an archived/alternate legitimate source where available;
- flag it for review.

YouTube videos and public web resources may disappear.
MAT should know the source existed even if the URL later fails.

============================================================

recommendations.title: FACT-LEVEL PROVENANCE
recommendations.text:
============================================================

For important quantitative facts, retain:

value
unit
quantity/property ID
conditions
temperature
pressure
phase
composition
isotope
measurement method
uncertainty
significant figures
source
evidence status
date/version
review state

Never treat:

"melting point = X"

as universally sufficient when X depends on pressure, phase,
composition or measurement definition.

This is essential for future simulation and materials synthesis.

============================================================

recommendations.title: MACHINE-READABLE MAT
recommendations.text:
============================================================

Human pagination must NEVER become the canonical data structure.

Every meaningful machine-readable object should have:

- stable MAT ID;
- type;
- label;
- relationships;
- provenance;
- evidence state;
- version;
- schema version;
- timestamps where relevant.

Provide structured exports where architecture permits:

JSON
YAML
JSON-LD
CSV for tabular extracts
EPUB for reading
HTML
print/PDF
potential API-ready publication model

Do not generate redundant authorities.

Generated exports must derive from canonical sources.

Prepare the architecture so a future MAT API can support queries such as:

"give all known phases of hydrogen at pressure P and temperature T"

"find materials satisfying a target conductivity and thermal range"

"show all claims relating element X to model Y"

"return only established or independently replicated evidence"

"return experimental failures involving process Z"

"show sources and uncertainty for this numerical property"

"traverse materials → processes → properties → applications"

============================================================

recommendations.title: PROFESSIONAL / INDUSTRY USE
recommendations.text:
============================================================

A specialist should be able to find their relevant information quickly.

Provide domain navigation/search/filtering rather than a giant static
profession list.

Examples:

chemist:
bonding, oxidation states, compounds, reactions, thermochemistry,
spectroscopy.

physicist:
electronic/nuclear/quantum states, fields, phase behavior, transport,
spectra, constants.

biologist:
biological role, biomolecules, pathways, organism/environment relevance.

medicine/pharma:
physiological relevance, isotopes/tracers, toxicology, diagnostics,
drug/material relationships — with appropriate medical-source quality
labels.

engineer:
material properties, tolerances, environmental dependence, processing,
manufacturing, failure modes, standards, applications.

technician:
measurement methods, practical tables, calibration, safety, procedures,
instrumentation.

AI/ML:
stable IDs, schemas, provenance, machine-readable relationships,
null semantics and confidence.

============================================================

recommendations.title: EDUCATION WITHOUT DUPLICATING THE SCIENCE
FIVE-STAR BOOK / CODEX READING EXPERIENCE
NAVIGATION
TRUE READING PAGINATION
TYPOGRAPHY / BOOK RHYTHM
VISUAL CONTENT SYSTEM
WALTER RUSSELL / ALTERNATIVE TABLE REFERENCES
IMAGE LABELS
recommendations.text:
============================================================

Audit captions underneath existing/reference images.

Captions must describe MAT's actual representation rather than blindly
reuse wording embedded in a source image.

Use:

Figure ID
Title
Description
Model/evidence lane
Source/inspiration where required
Rights/attribution
Alt text
Relationship to canonical MAT entities

============================================================

recommendations.title: SEARCH
recommendations.text:
============================================================

Search should eventually span:

elements
symbols
MAT IDs
properties
compounds
materials
processes
applications
people
authors
papers
books
patents
datasets
experiments
models
claims
industries/domains
sources
citations
keywords

Add filter facets where useful:

evidence
domain
source type
record type
review status
date
property
phase
availability

Do not overload the default search UI.

============================================================

recommendations.title: READER TOOLS
HOVER / TAP INTERACTION
EXPERT REVIEW SYSTEM
CORRECTIONS AND CONTRIBUTIONS
ACCESSIBILITY
RESPONSIVE DESIGN
recommendations.text:
============================================================

Desktop:
may use margins, side citations and multi-column support areas.

Tablet:
retain book identity without squeezing side panels.

Phone:
single primary reading column.

Do not shrink desktop UI until it technically fits.

Recompose it.

Navigation should become drawers/sheets/compact controls.

Data tables should have deliberate mobile behavior.

============================================================

recommendations.title: PERFORMANCE / OFFLINE
DATA VISUALIZATION QUALITY
MEDICAL / SAFETY CONTENT
PATENTS / REDACTED / HARD-TO-ACCESS SOURCES
CROSS-REFERENCE ENGINE
recommendations.text:
============================================================

Support explicit typed relations such as:

IS_ISOTOPE_OF
ION_OF
COMPOUND_CONTAINS
BONDS_WITH
REACTS_WITH
TRANSFORMS_TO
PHASE_OF
ALLOTROPE_OF
PRODUCED_BY
USED_IN
MEASURED_BY
HAS_SPECTRUM
HAS_PROPERTY
DEPENDS_ON
CITED_BY
SUPPORTED_BY
CONTRADICTED_BY
PROPOSED_BY
DISCOVERED_BY
RELATED_TO
PART_OF
APPLIED_IN
HAZARD_IN
BIOLOGICAL_ROLE
HISTORICAL_MODEL_OF

Reuse the existing MAT relationship architecture when possible.

Do not introduce another incompatible graph system.

============================================================

recommendations.title: PEOPLE / INTELLECTUAL LINEAGE
recommendations.text:
============================================================

Create/strengthen a structured People directory.

A person should be linkable from anywhere in MAT.

Separate:

A. historical/scientific contributors;
B. authors of cited publications;
C. inventors/patent holders;
D. MAT contributors/reviewers;
E. people associated with unconventional/historical claims.

Person pages/records may contain:

name
dates
fields
organizations
known contributions
related MAT records
works
patents
sources
external authority links
evidence/context notes

Avoid biographies becoming unsourced editorial claims.

============================================================

recommendations.title: BOOK INDEXING
CONTENT DUPLICATION RULE
recommendations.text:
============================================================

Do not copy a canonical density value into ten profession pages as ten
separate truths.

Reference the same fact.

Domain-specific prose may explain its significance differently.

Example:

canonical:
hydrogen property X = value + unit + conditions + source.

aerospace lens:
explains why property X matters to storage/propulsion engineering.

cryogenics lens:
explains why property X matters at low temperature.

The factual object remains one object.

============================================================

recommendations.title: RECORD DIRECTORY REVIEW
recommendations.text:
============================================================

Do not blindly replace the existing:

calculations/
data/
diagrams/
experiments/
graphs/
images/
models/
relationships/
sources/
tables/

This organization is valuable.

Determine whether a complementary structure is needed for:

domains/
narrative/
claims/
citations/
reviews/

Before adding physical directories, decide whether each should instead
be represented through metadata/registries/generated views.

Prefer architecture over folder proliferation.

Document the decision.

============================================================

recommendations.title: FRONTEND VS BACKEND
recommendations.text:
============================================================

Strictly separate:

CANONICAL KNOWLEDGE
from
PUBLICATION PROJECTION
from
USER STATE.

Canonical scientific records:
repository-controlled.

Generated publication:
rebuildable.

Reader state such as bookmarks/notes/position:
local/user-controlled unless a future optional account service is
introduced.

Do NOT require an account to read MAT.

============================================================

recommendations.title: BOOK VS STUDIO
recommendations.text:
============================================================

Do not confuse MAT Studio with the public reader.

STUDIO:
authoring, review, data inspection, export, publication workflow.

PUBLIC READER:
calm, beautiful, low-friction reading/reference experience.

A normal reader should not see authoring controls unless explicitly
entering an editing/contribution environment.

Audit whether this separation is currently clear enough.

============================================================

recommendations.title: COMPARE EBOOKCRAFT TO MAT
PROFESSIONAL BENCHMARK REVIEW
recommendations.text:
============================================================

Score the current MAT before changes from 1–5 for:

scientific data architecture
scientific provenance
research usefulness
chemist usefulness
physicist usefulness
biology usefulness
medical/pharma usefulness
engineering usefulness
technician usefulness
education usefulness
general-reader usefulness
AI/ML usefulness
knowledge-graph maturity
citations
search/retrieval
book/editorial quality
narrative/history
navigation
typography
visual hierarchy
data visualization
accessibility
mobile UX
tablet UX
desktop UX
print/PDF
EPUB
offline capability
performance
maintainability
extensibility

For every score below 5:
state the concrete reason and required fix.

Repeat the benchmark after implementation.

Do not claim 5/5 unless measurable acceptance criteria are satisfied.

============================================================

recommendations.title: IMPLEMENTATION PRIORITY
TESTING
VISUAL REGRESSION
DO NOT HIDE SCIENTIFIC COMPLEXITY
recommendations.text:
============================================================

Progressive disclosure means:

simple first view
+
deeper specialist access.

It does NOT mean deleting complexity.

MAT should be capable of going deeper than a normal textbook while
remaining readable at entry level.

============================================================

recommendations.title: README / DOCUMENTATION UPDATE
COMPLETION REPORT
recommendations.text:
============================================================

At the end give me:

A. Executive review of the original MAT.
B. Exact architectural problems found.
C. Exact files changed.
D. Exact files added.
E. Exact migrations performed.
F. Data-completeness matrix.
G. Broken/weak source report.
H. Internal/external link report.
I. UI/UX benchmark before and after.
J. Accessibility result.
K. Build/test results.
L. Before/after screenshot locations.
M. Remaining image-generation requirements.
N. Remaining scientific-data gaps.
O. Remaining expert-review requirements.
P. Recommended next production record/element.
Q. Git diff summary.
R. Commit hashes.

Do not report a test as passed unless you actually executed it.

============================================================

recommendations.title: STOP CONDITIONS
START FROM THE CURRENT REPOSITORY
recommendations.text:
Run:

```bash
git status
git pull --ff-only
git log -10 --oneline
```

Do not assume this prompt's commit is still current.

At the time of external audit, main was at approximately:

`f9f8109`

but the local repository may now be newer.

Preserve all legitimate work added since then.

---

recommendations.title: THE CURRENT APPLICATION IS NOT COMPLETE
recommendations.text:
Do not treat the existing MAT Studio as finished.

External audit has already found:

1. `studio/src/components/LivePreview.tsx`
   is effectively a placeholder.

2. `studio/src/components/Inspector.tsx`
   contains hard-coded zero values instead of actual MAT record data.

3. Studio loads a manifest directly rather than consuming a properly designed Studio/publication model.

4. Book/Data/Preview/Validate/Export currently resemble navigation tabs more than complete workflows.

5. The root GitHub workflow does not properly install/build/test the Studio.

6. The 118-element dataset contains `MAT:null` entries and scientifically unsafe placeholder-style data.

7. Latest validation is also failing because Carbon references source IDs that are absent from the source registry.

Do NOT hide these problems.

Fix each category properly.

---

recommendations.title: FIRST GOAL — MAKE THE PROGRAM ACTUALLY WORK
recommendations.text:
Before improving appearance:

make Studio boot reliably.

Required development workflow:

```bash
npm install
npm run studio
```

from the repository root.

The root command must:

1. prepare required generated MAT data;
2. make that data available to Studio;
3. install/use correct Studio dependencies;
4. start Studio;
5. report useful errors if preparation fails.

Prefer npm workspaces or another clean package strategy.

Do not require the user to manually run five undocumented commands.

Add:

```bash
npm run studio
npm run build:studio
npm run test:studio
npm run check:studio
```

Make them real.

---

recommendations.title: ADD STUDIO TO CI
recommendations.text:
The current CI must not ignore the application that the user actually sees.

Create separate logical CI stages/jobs if necessary:

```text
SCIENTIFIC VALIDATION
BOOK BUILD
BOOK TESTS
STUDIO BUILD
STUDIO TESTS
PUBLICATION MODEL
GENERATED-FILE SYNC
```

Important:

The existing Carbon source errors must remain visible.

However, a scientific validation failure should not prevent us from discovering that the Studio itself does not compile.

Use separate jobs where appropriate.

Never weaken scientific validation to get a green check.

---

recommendations.title: DO NOT INVENT THE MISSING CARBON SOURCES
recommendations.text:
There are references around:

```text
SRC-000084
SRC-000086
SRC-000087
SRC-000088
SRC-000089
SRC-000090
```

that currently do not resolve.

Investigate them.

If legitimate source information exists elsewhere in repository history or documentation, recover and register it.

If not:

leave an explicit unresolved-source error.

DO NOT create fake:

- titles
- authors
- journals
- DOI numbers
- URLs
- dates

just to make CI green.

---

recommendations.title: REBUILD THE 118-ELEMENT BASELINE
recommendations.text:
This is now a priority.

The user wants every currently recognised chemical element available immediately so they can progressively overwrite/extend each record later.

There are 118 recognised elements.

Create stable MAT IDs:

```text
Hydrogen    MAT:0001
Helium      MAT:0002
...
Neon        MAT:0010
...
Oganesson   MAT:0118
```

There must NEVER again be:

```json
"matId": "MAT:null"
```

for a recognised element.

MAT:0000 remains Origin State and is NOT a chemical element.

---

recommendations.title: BASELINE IS NOT THE SAME AS CURATED
recommendations.text:
Introduce explicit status.

For example:

```json
{
  "recordStatus": "BASELINE"
}
```

versus:

```json
{
  "recordStatus": "CURATED"
}
```

Current detailed MAT records 0001–0009 can remain:

`CURATED`

or another appropriate existing status.

Elements 0010–0118 become:

`BASELINE`

until individually completed.

Potential states:

```text
BASELINE
IN-PROGRESS
CURATED
REVIEWED
PUBLISHED
DEPRECATED
```

Use existing MAT vocabulary if one already exists.

Do not introduce redundant status systems.

---

recommendations.title: BASELINE ELEMENT DATA MUST BE REAL DATA
recommendations.text:
Replace the current unsourced 118-element placeholder file with a properly sourced baseline catalogue.

Use authoritative sources.

Preferred source hierarchy:

### Identity and general element data

PubChem Periodic Table / Element data.

PubChem exposes machine-readable/downloadable element data and identifies sources including IUPAC, NIST, IAEA and other scientific authorities.

### Standard atomic weights

CIAAW / IUPAC 2024 standard atomic-weight table.

Important:

Do not convert intervals into fake single exact values.

Preserve things such as:

```text
[1.00784, 1.00811]
```

where the standard atomic weight is an interval.

### Ground electronic configuration and ionization energy

NIST Atomic Spectra Database 5.12 where appropriate.

### Nuclear/isotope information

Use established evaluated nuclear sources already accepted by MAT where appropriate.

---

recommendations.title: DOWNLOAD ONCE — DO NOT REQUIRE INTERNET AT RUNTIME
recommendations.text:
Create an ingestion/update pipeline such as:

```text
scripts/sync-elements-baseline.mjs
```

The script may retrieve authoritative upstream data when deliberately run.

The normal MAT book and Studio must NOT require PubChem/NIST/IUPAC network access to start.

Store the resulting reviewed snapshot in the repository.

Example:

```text
data/catalog/elements-baseline.yaml
```

or the closest architecturally appropriate location.

The snapshot must contain provenance.

Example:

```yaml
catalog:
  id: MAT:ELEMENTS:BASELINE
  version: ...
  updated: ...
  sources:
    - ...

elements:
  - mat_id: MAT:0010
    atomic_number: 10
    symbol: Ne
    name: Neon
    period: 2
    group: 18
    block: p
    classification: noble-gas

    atomic_weight:
      display: "20.1797(6)"
      source_ids:
        - ...

    electron_configuration:
      value: ...
      source_ids:
        - ...

    first_ionization_energy:
      value: ...
      unit: eV
      uncertainty: ...
      source_ids:
        - ...

    record_status: BASELINE
```

Adapt to MAT's actual schema.

---

recommendations.title: REMOVE FAKE PLACEHOLDER SCIENCE
recommendations.text:
Audit the current:

`book/data/elements-118.json`

especially elements approximately Z >= 90.

Values such as:

```text
universeAbundance: 0.000001
crustAbundance: 0.1
humanAbundance: 0.000001
```

repeated across synthetic elements must NOT remain unless an actual source supports them.

The same applies to:

```text
phase: Solid
phase: Gas
electronConfiguration: "[Core] + 118e⁻"
```

and arbitrary atomic masses.

Replace unsupported data with MAT null ontology.

For example:

```yaml
value: null
null_reason: UNAVAILABLE
```

or:

```yaml
value: null
null_reason: UNKNOWN
```

or:

```yaml
value: null
null_reason: NOT_APPLICABLE
```

depending on the established MAT schema.

Never use zero as a substitute for unknown.

Never use a tiny fake number as a substitute for unknown.

---

recommendations.title: DISTINGUISH MEASURED FROM PREDICTED
recommendations.text:
This is especially important for superheavy elements.

Where properties are theoretical/predicted rather than experimentally established, represent that explicitly.

Example:

```yaml
evidence_type: PREDICTED
```

not:

```yaml
evidence_type: MEASURED
```

If the baseline source does not establish the property reliably:

leave it unknown.

MAT values scientific honesty over filling every box.

---

recommendations.title: BASIC DATA PACKAGE FOR ALL 118
recommendations.text:
Each baseline record should support, where authoritative information exists:

```text
MAT ID
atomic number
symbol
name
period
group
block
broad element classification
standard atomic weight / representative atomic mass
standard state, if authoritative
ground-state electron configuration
first ionization energy
electronegativity where defined
atomic radius WITH radius definition
melting point where known
boiling point where known
density WITH conditions/reference state
discovery year where supported
oxidation states where supported
basic source/provenance identifiers
record status
```

Do not force unavailable fields.

Condition-sensitive quantities require:

```text
value
unit
conditions
definition/method
source
uncertainty where available
```

---

recommendations.title: DO NOT CREATE 109 FAKE FULL RESEARCH RECORDS
recommendations.text:
Elements 0010–0118 do not need hundreds of empty files each yet.

Create a lightweight baseline record system.

The hierarchy should be:

```text
BASELINE ELEMENT CATALOGUE
        +
OPTIONAL CURATED MAT RECORD
        ↓
MERGED PUBLICATION VIEW
```

The curated record takes precedence when present.

Example:

```text
MAT:0010 Neon
baseline catalogue
       ↓
user later creates records/0010-Neon-Ne/
       ↓
curated fields extend/override the baseline for publication
```

Do not destroy baseline provenance when an override occurs.

---

recommendations.title: EVERY ELEMENT MUST BE SELECTABLE
recommendations.text:
This is a non-negotiable UX requirement.

Every one of the 118 periodic-table cells must be:

- keyboard focusable;
- mouse clickable;
- touch selectable;
- screen-reader labelled.

Do not mark elements 10–118:

```html
aria-disabled="true"
```

merely because their detailed MAT record has not been written yet.

Use a proper:

```html
<button>
```

or navigable link.

---

recommendations.title: PERIODIC TABLE ROUTING
recommendations.text:

### CURATED

Hydrogen through whichever records currently have full MAT content:

open the full MAT record.

### BASELINE

For an element without a full record:

open its generated baseline element page.

Example:

```text
MAT:0010
NEON
BASELINE REFERENCE
```

with its verified data.

Prominent banner:

```text
BASELINE ELEMENT RECORD

This element is available for reference and navigation but has not yet received the full MAT curated record package.
```

Do not call baseline data “incomplete” in a way that suggests the known facts are unreliable.

Do not invent content.

- symbol;

recommendations.title: REBUILD STUDIO TO FEEL LIKE AN ACTUAL EBOOK AUTHORING APPLICATION
recommendations.text:

The implementation is not.

Transform it into:

```text
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
```

recommendations.title: FIX THE PUBLICATION MODEL
recommendations.text:

`scripts/build-publication-model.mjs`

It currently needs strengthening.

Do not hard-code scientific glossary definitions with inappropriate source IDs.

Do not attach Origin State sources to unrelated scientific definitions merely to populate a source field.

Generate glossary entries from canonical controlled data where possible.

If a term lacks a verified source:

mark it accordingly rather than inventing provenance.

recommendations.title: FIX CHART DATASET KEY MISMATCHES
recommendations.text:

`book/data/chart-datasets.json`


Likewise inspect:

```text

crust
```

Add tests.

recommendations.text:

Then copy/expose them safely to Studio during:


Do not make Studio randomly fetch files that Vite does not serve.

recommendations.title: PUBLICATION MODEL SHOULD INCLUDE BASELINE ELEMENTS
recommendations.text:
The generated publication model must contain all 118 elements.

Example:

```json

  "atomicNumber": 10,
  "symbol": "Ne",
  "name": "Neon",
  "recordStatus": "BASELINE",
  "fullRecord": false
}
```

Full records then contain:

```json

  "mat": "MAT:0001",
  "recordStatus": "CURATED",
  "fullRecord": true,
  "recordPath": "records/0001-Hydrogen-H/..."
}
```

It may instead report:

```text

```

Do not simply silence the warning.

recommendations.title: DON'T OVERWRITE USER SCIENCE
recommendations.text:
When a curated record exists:

Merge precedence:

```text

      ↓

      ↓
UNKNOWN
```

But always retain provenance for whichever value is rendered.

Detect conflicting values and report them.

Do not silently resolve scientific disagreements.

recommendations.text:

Example for Neon:

```text
records/0010-Neon-Ne/
```

using the current master MAT record template.

Seed only approved baseline identity/basic values.

Generate structured placeholders for the remainder.

Do not generate fake isotope/spectrum/material data.

Do not overwrite an existing folder.

recommendations.title: MAKE THE USER'S LATER WORK EASY
recommendations.text:
The user's intended workflow is:

```text

→ see baseline Neon data
→ Create/expand full record
→ overwrite/add specialised MAT information
→ validate
→ preview
→ publish
```

Design around this.

Do not force them to manually create every base identity from scratch.

recommendations.text:
Studio should feel intentionally designed.

Use a professional dark authoring workspace around a warm/light book canvas.

Example:


- search;
- charts;
- reading tools;
- publication UI;
- translation;
- TTS.

recommendations.title: DO NOT DESTROY CURRENT WORK
recommendations.text:
Before refactoring:


Recommended commits:

```text

add authoritative 118-element baseline catalogue
enable all-element navigation
```

At minimum run:

```bash
npm run build:book
```

recommendations.title: FINAL REPORT
recommendations.text:
Return:

### Fixed
Actual failures repaired.

### 118-element baseline
Source/data architecture and counts.

### Studio
Which workflows now function.

### Reader
Which navigation/features changed.

### Scientific integrity
Anything intentionally left unresolved.

### CI
Exact results.

Exact files created/changed.

Do not say “done” unless the application was actually run and tested.

---

PRIMARY RESULT REQUIRED:

When this work is complete I must be able to:

1. launch MAT Studio;
2. see all 118 elements;
3. click any element;
4. view basic source-backed information immediately;
5. distinguish baseline from fully curated records;
6. open Hydrogen's complete MAT material;
7. open Oganesson as a baseline record;
8. use a real EbookCraft-style Write → Design → Data → Review → Preview → Export workflow;
9. see a real book page in the centre;
10. see real data in Inspector;
11. later promote any baseline element into a full MAT record without starting from zero.

Do not stop at another mock-up.

Build the functioning workflow.

One additional recommendation is important: **do not create 109 giant “empty” record folders right now.** The baseline-catalogue approach gives you all 118 selectable elements immediately while keeping the repository manageable. When you choose “Create full MAT record” for, say, Gold (`MAT:0079`), the system can then generate the complete locked folder/template package and inherit Gold's verified baseline data.

That gives you the workflow you were originally aiming for: **browse everything now, deepen each element later, without losing scientific provenance or having to rebuild the book architecture each time.**

policy: Original documents retained unchanged. Embedded roles, commands, branching and commit requests are source text, not executed instructions. Historical findings must be checked against the current checkout.
